name: chamfer_angle_changes_in_deg
why: ENTRY Z-C21.2, finding M3. set_dimension converted every dimension from millimetres: «30» on the angle of a chamfer became 0.03 rad, that is 1.7 degrees, and the re-reading — converted the same way — said it had taken. IDimension~GetType.html: «Type of dimension as defined by swDimensionParamType_e» (DoubleAngular = 1). The state writes angular dimensions in degrees: now set_dimension reads and writes them in degrees, and the answer says so with «before_deg» and «after_deg».
defect_caught: The 5 at 45 degrees chamfer of `chamfer_5_at_45`, then the angle brought to 30. On the old library the answer has «before_mm» and «now_mm» (0.785 and 30 «mm» on a dimension in radians) and no «after_deg»: the case is red at the first expectation.
_the_dimension_is_named_by_kind: `@dimension(angular=true)`: the only dimension in degrees of the part, which the state marks with «deg». The names SOLIDWORKS gives to the dimensions of a chamfer (D1, D2) and their order are not measured, and writing them here would be guessing.
_why_there_is_no_volume: With one side of 5 and the angle at 30 degrees the other side is 5 x tan 30 = 2.887 or 5 / tan 30 = 8.660, depending on which face SOLIDWORKS counts the angle from, and this is not measured: 119278.31 or 117834.94 mm3. An expectation on one of the two numbers would be a bet; the dimension re-read in degrees is not.

expect.why: re-read from the dimension and converted to degrees. On the old library the field is not there
the angle of the chamfer as it was: 45 degrees, not 0.785
